title: A reply a layer answered still confirms the token the end-point has already issued

provenance.quote: Either the client agent or the server agent may be the first one to create a submessage with format field of 'token' and the subformat field starting with 'conversation'. ... The intent is to maintain the concept of a continuous conversation among the two agents.

notes: `ecma-430/30`'s pair of halves — §6.2's exception takes the end-point's own token out of the echo, §6.2.1's confirmation puts it back exactly once — read on a reply no handler produced. The reading is `readings/51`'s: the obligation is about the reply the peer receives, so a layer that answers on its own owes the confirmation a handler would have owed, and a peer whose conversation is served from a cache must not see the identifier it is holding disappear for a turn. `ecma-430/31` is the same assertion on the ordinary path and the two must agree; that they do is what says the confirmation is in the idempotent half of clause 6 (`Conformity::close`) rather than in the step that finishes a handler's answer.
